items.title: The Design of Everyday Things (Revised and Expanded Edition)
items.why: The book that made affordance, signifier and feedback part of every designer's vocabulary, and the habit of blaming the design before the user.

items.title: Don't Make Me Think, Revisited
items.why: A short, funny book on web and mobile usability that you can read in an evening and use the next morning.

items.title: The Elements of User Experience
items.why: The five planes model, from strategy to surface, which helps you see which layer a problem really lives on.

items.title: Refactoring UI
items.why: Specific visual design tactics explained from a developer's point of view, ideal for someone who builds first and designs second.

items.title: Practical UI
items.why: Quick, actionable rules for interface design with little theory, from a product designer with nearly two decades of UI work.

items.title: Laws of UX (2nd edition)
items.why: The psychology behind interfaces in book form; the second edition adds more on the psychology behind each principle and updated examples.

items.title: Thinking with Type (3rd edition)
items.why: A clear, visual guide to letters, text and grids, from typefaces and kerning to how paragraphs should be spaced and aligned.

items.title: Interaction of Color (50th Anniversary Edition)
items.why: A classic set of exercises showing that a colour changes with its neighbours, the root of most palette and contrast surprises.

items.title: Writing Is Designing
items.by: Michael J. Metts and Andy Welfle
items.why: How to give people clarity through interface words, test them and work with your team on them as part of the design.

items.title: Mismatch: How Inclusion Shapes Design
items.why: A short book on how designs exclude people by accident, and how designing with excluded people produces better products for everyone.

items.title: Designing Interface Animation
items.why: A crash course in motion for web designers, on using animation for feedback, orientation, attention and cause and effect.

items.title: Atomic Design
items.why: A way to build interfaces from small parts up to full pages, free to read online, and a widely used introduction to thinking in design systems.

items.title: Information Dashboard Design (2nd edition)
items.why: Stephen Few's detailed guide to the common problems in dashboard design and the best practices that fix them, with many examples.

items.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (2nd edition)
items.why: The classic on charts and tables, where ideas such as the data-ink ratio and chartjunk come from.

items.title: NN/g (Nielsen Norman Group)
items.why: Short, research-based videos on almost every UX topic, most under five minutes; the safest first stop when you want the evidence behind a design rule.

items.title: Apple Developer
items.why: The WWDC design sessions, such as the yearly design principles talks, explain how Apple's own designers think; skip the coding sessions and search for 'design'.

items.title: Figma
items.why: Config conference talks and the free Introduction to design systems course; the best source for how working teams build components and tokens.

items.title: Flux Academy
items.why: Long, well-made lessons on web design fundamentals such as grids, hierarchy, colour and type, aimed at people who build sites for real clients.

items.title: Sajid
items.why: Opinionated, practical UI videos on spacing, colour, type and depth, each one a method you can apply to a screen the same day.

items.title: Pimp my Type
items.why: Oliver Schöndorfer's channel on typography for web and product interfaces, from line length to font pairing to contrast; clear and grounded in real projects.

items.title: Linus Boman
items.why: Thoughtful video essays on typography, logos and legibility; the one to watch when you want to train your eye for letterforms and the history behind them.

items.title: Kevin Powell
items.why: A patient, clear CSS teacher with a good eye for design; useful when you need to understand what your AI tool's CSS is actually doing.

items.title: Learn UI Design
items.why: Erik Kennedy's practical UI lessons on colour, typography, layout and process; the video side of the Learn UI Design blog used in the colour and spacing lessons.

items.title: The Futur
items.why: Mostly about the business of creative work, with some excellent short design theory lessons on colour and type tucked in; search the channel for those.

items.title: Mizko
items.why: Figma-based tutorials on spacing systems, type scales, grids and design systems; good when you want to see a system built step by step.

items.title: NN/G UX Podcast
items.why: Nielsen Norman Group's researchers and guests on one UX topic per episode, from icons to interviews; reliable and free of hype.

items.title: Design Better
items.why: Long interviews with designers, researchers and authors such as Steve Portigal and Jake Knapp; strong on process and the thinking behind good products.

items.title: Complementary
items.why: Two working interface designers, Anthony Hobday and Katie Langerman, take one interface topic per episode (layout, colour, forms, materials); the closest match to this course.

items.title: Dive Club
items.why: Ridd's interviews with today's product designers on craft, tools and design engineering; good for hearing how current product teams actually work.

items.title: 99% Invisible
items.why: Stories about the design of everyday things, from doors to flags to cities; builds the habit of noticing design decisions everywhere.

items.title: Design Matters with Debbie Millman
items.why: One of the longest-running design interview shows, with type designers, graphic designers and writers; better for philosophy and careers than for interface technique.

items.title: Design Notes
items.why: Hosted by a Google UX designer, with many episodes on the making of Material Design and award-winning apps alongside interviews from wider creative fields.

items.title: Twenty Thousand Hertz
items.why: Stories about designed sound, from alert tones to car clicks; the best way to start thinking about audio feedback in the products you build.

items.title: Awkward Silences
items.why: A show about user research from the team at User Interviews; useful each time you plan to talk to your users and want better questions.

items.title: Rosenfeld Review Podcast
items.why: Lou Rosenfeld, co-author of the classic information architecture book, talks with UX authors such as Steve Krug and Abby Covert; short and practical.

items.title: WebAIM Contrast Checker
items.why: Paste two colours and see at once whether they pass WCAG AA and AAA for normal text, large text and interface parts.

items.title: Who Can Use
items.why: Shows how a colour pair looks to people with different kinds of colour blindness and low vision, and roughly how many people that affects.

items.title: Realtime Colors
items.why: Try a palette and fonts on a realistic web page, flip between light and dark, then export the colours as CSS and other formats. Free.

items.title: Huemint
items.why: Generates colour palettes with machine learning and previews them on brand and website mockups.

items.title: OKLCH Color Picker & Converter
items.why: Pick colours in OKLCH, where equal steps in lightness look equal to the eye, and convert them to the formats your code needs.

items.title: Accessible Palette
items.why: Builds colour scales with consistent lightness and contrast across hues, so every shade at the same step behaves the same way.

items.title: Coolors
items.why: A fast palette generator for exploring combinations, locking the colours you like and shuffling the rest.

items.title: Typescale
items.why: Choose a base size and ratio, preview the whole type scale with real fonts, and copy the CSS.

items.title: Utopia
items.why: Generates fluid type and spacing scales that grow smoothly with the screen, with fewer breakpoints to manage.

items.title: Google Fonts
items.why: A large library of free, open-licence typefaces with live previews, ready to use on the web.

items.title: Figma
items.why: The standard interface design tool, with a free Starter plan that is enough for sketching layouts and building a small component library.

items.title: Lucide
items.why: A consistent open-source icon set with matching stroke widths and corners, easy to use in code.

items.title: Phosphor Icons
items.why: A flexible icon family in several weights, useful when you need icons to match the weight of your type.

items.title: Mobbin
items.why: A searchable library of real screens and flows from shipped apps and websites, free to join, for seeing how others solve the same pattern.

items.title: Laws of UX
items.why: Illustrated cards for the psychology principles behind interfaces, handy as a quick reference while you design.

items.title: cubic-bezier.com
items.why: Drag the handles of an easing curve, compare it against standard easings and copy the value into your CSS.

items.title: Land-book
items.why: A hand-picked, daily-updated gallery of websites you can filter by page type, such as landing, pricing or about pages.

items.title: Siteinspire
items.why: A long-running showcase of well-crafted websites, filterable by style, type and subject.

items.title: SaaS Landing Page
items.why: Landing, pricing, features and FAQ pages from software companies, useful when you are designing the same page for your own product.

items.title: Refero
items.why: Real product screens, flows and patterns from web and iOS apps, organised by page type such as onboarding, pricing and dashboards.

items.title: Awwwards
items.why: Award-winning, often experimental websites, best for stretching your eye on type, layout and motion more than for copying patterns.

items.title: Minimal Gallery
items.why: Hand-picked websites with restrained, minimal design, good for studying space, type and hierarchy with few distractions.

items.title: Dark Design
items.why: A gallery of dark-themed websites, helpful for seeing how good sites handle contrast and colour in dark mode.
